Bug in my reference's `vi()`: after reading the first byte, `self.p` was already incremented, so the remaining bytes are at `self.p + i - 1` for i in 1..w-1, and then `self.p += w-1`.

In Java: `for (int i = 1; i < width; i++) v = (v << 8) | (data[p++] & 255L);` — increments p each time ✓.

In Python I wrote:
```python
        b=self.d[self.p]; self.p+=1
        w=1<<(b>>6)
        if w-1>len(self.d)-self.p: raise Err(...)
        val=b&0x3f
        for i in range(1,w): val=(val<<8)|self.d[self.p+i]
        self.p+=w-1
```
So for i in 1..w-1, the byte is at self.p + i - 1 (since p already advanced past the first byte). I wrote `self.d[self.p+i]` — off by one. Fix: `self.d[self.p+i-1]`.

Let me fix.
